items.summary: Fix Modern Word comment reporting with NVDA+alt+c and Elements List (#20894)
items.fullMessage:
Fix Modern Word comment reporting with NVDA+alt+c and Elements List (#20894)

Fixes #14985
Fixes #9685
Related to #4336
Summary of the issue:

With UI Automation, Word exposes each comment as a comment thread. NVDA reads the name of the thread, which is Word's localized "Comment thread started by ". The comment text and the replies are never reported, neither by NVDA+alt+c nor in the Elements List. Resolved threads are missing from the Elements List.
With classic comments (Enable modern comments disabled in Word's General settings), NVDA+alt+c only reads the first comment, and its replies are listed as separate comments.
Description of user facing changes:

In Microsoft Word accessed via UI Automation, NVDA+alt+c reports the text of the comment, followed by each reply with its author and date. Each of them is spoken as a separate utterance. Pressing the command twice shows the comment and its replies in a browsable message.
In the Elements List, annotations show the text of the comment. Replies are listed under the comment they reply to. Resolved comments in the modern experience are listed and reported as resolved. A comment whose text has several formatting runs is listed once.
Description of developer facing changes:

getCommentInfoFromPosition and getPresentableCommentInfoFromPosition in NVDAObjects.UIA.wordDocument are deprecated. They still return the dictionary and the text they returned before.
Description of development approach:

Modern Word exposes a comment thread as a tree item with the annotation pattern. Its full description is the text of the first comment. Its annotation author and date belong to that comment. Each reply is a child tree item with its own annotation pattern, full description, author and date. The annotation object on the commented text is the thread, or one of its replies when comments are shown in the margin.

Classic comments have the same structure with other elements. Each comment is a group with the annotation pattern, and its replies are nested groups. The annotation object on the commented text is the edit field in the group of a comment. The full description of a group is empty, so the text of the comment comes from that edit field.

A private _getCommentInfoFromPosition finds the thread from the annotation object. When the annotation object is the edit field of a classic comment, the comment is its parent. When the comment is a reply, the thread is its parent. One cache request then fetches the thread and all its replies. The result is a private dataclass, _CommentInfo, which also defines how to present the comment to the user. This replaces the fallback that read the author and date of a classic comment from the names of neighbouring elements.

The thread element does not tell whether it is resolved. Only the annotation types of the commented text do, through Word's custom ResolvedComment annotation type. The Elements List item already has these annotation types, so it passes them on. NVDA+alt+c reads them from the caret.

In the Elements List, comment items also match Word's ResolvedComment annotation type. That type only gets its ID at runtime, so the comment item mixes in AutoPropertyObject to make wantedAttribValues a class property. After comments and revisions are merged, a reply item follows each comment. A reply only nests under its own comment, and other annotations never nest under a reply. Replies are only fetched when the list moves past a comment, so replies never become quick navigation stops.

The annotation iterator yields one comment item for each formatting run of the commented text. When the thread is fetched, _CommentInfo also keeps the runtime ID of the thread element. A comment item is skipped, together with its replies, when its thread has the same runtime ID as that of the previous comment item. The comparison starts at the second comment item. Quick navigation only takes the first item, so it fetches nothing extra.
